mcq.question: What makes `PaymentMethod` an abstract class?

options.B: It declares at least one pure virtual function (`= 0`)

mcq.explanation: A class with a pure virtual function cannot be instantiated; only derived classes that override every pure virtual function can be.

mcq.question: Why does `PaymentMethod` need a virtual destructor?

options.A: So that deleting a derived object through a base-class pointer runs the derived destructor
options.C: Otherwise derived classes cannot be copied

mcq.explanation: Without a virtual destructor, `delete base_ptr` only runs the base destructor and the behaviour is undefined. `unique_ptr<PaymentMethod>` relies on this.
